name: Lume
description:
A lightweight Spotlight-style search window for GNOME Shell: apps, files, windows, settings, calculator, unit and currency conversion, emoji, snippets, media, quick toggles, processes, web search and more. Opens with Super+Alt+Space.

Clipboard access: Lume keeps a clipboard history (it can be turned off, and is saved to disk only if you choose). Snippets, calculator and clipboard results can be copied to the clipboard and pasted into the window you were using.

Network access: weather and time-zone searches send the city to Open-Meteo.com as you type; currency conversion downloads ECB exchange rates from frankfurter.dev. Offline Mode stops these, results from apps' search providers and web search rows. Commands, AI agents and web addresses you choose to open are not affected.

Commands: when you choose a result, Lume runs the command you typed (in your terminal by default) or an AI agent CLI in your terminal. Executables you put in ~/.config/lume/scripts run when you type their name, to produce results. Nothing runs with elevated privileges.
